title: Constraint
description: One limit the user placed on what the agent may do. Constraints are carried by an open mandate and evaluated by the verifier against the closed mandate the agent presents — never by the agent, which is what makes the design safe against a model that proposes anything it likes. The vocabulary is ours; AP2 merely transports it. The type registry, the per-type parameter schemas and the evaluators are defined in internal/core/authz/constraint (#11).

type.description: Identifier of the constraint type, e.g. 'price.max' or 'temporal.window'. Deliberately not an enum: an unknown constraint type must be representable so that the verifier can reject it explicitly and say so in a receipt. Closing the set here would turn that into a parse failure instead, which cannot be receipted and cannot be told apart from a malformed message.

params.description: Parameters for this constraint type, interpreted by the evaluator registered for it. Open by construction — the registry, not this schema, decides what is valid for a given type.
